passages.text: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “What do you people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge’?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He said these words to me.
He asked about the people of Israel.
He said, “Why do you use this proverb in Israel?”
The people say, ‘The fathers have eaten sour grapes.’
They say, ‘The children’s teeth are set on edge.’”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ מַה־ לָּכֶ֗ם אַתֶּם֙ מֹֽשְׁלִים֙ אֶת־ הַמָּשָׁ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־ אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD is alive.
The Lord GOD makes a promise.
The Lord GOD says to Israel, “You will not use this proverb anymore.”
No one in Israel will say this saying again.
passages.original: חַי־ אָ֕נִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה אִם־ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם ע֗וֹד מְשֹׁ֛ל הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Behold, every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says that every soul belongs to Him.
God owns the soul of the father.
God owns the soul of the son.
God says each soul is His.
God says the soul that sins will die.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן כָּל־ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת֙ לִ֣י הֵ֔נָּה כְּנֶ֧פֶשׁ הָאָ֛ב וּכְנֶ֥פֶשׁ הַבֵּ֖ן לִי־ הֵ֑נָּה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת׃ס

passages.text: Now suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife or approach a woman during her period.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man lives among the people of Israel.
This man does what is just.
He does what is right.
He does not eat at the mountain shrines.
He does not look to the idols of Israel.
He does not defile his neighbor’s wife.
He does not approach a woman during her period.
passages.original: וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי־ יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃ אֶל־ הֶֽהָרִים֙ לֹ֣א אָכָ֔ל וְעֵינָיו֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔א אֶל־ גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאֶת־ אֵ֤שֶׁת רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ לֹ֣א טִמֵּ֔א וְאֶל־ אִשָּׁ֥ה נִדָּ֖ה לֹ֥א יִקְרָֽב׃

passages.text: He does not oppress another, but restores the pledge to the debtor. He does not commit robbery, but gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man does not oppress others.
He returns a pledge to the person who owes him.
He does not steal.
He gives his bread to the hungry.
He covers the naked with clothing.
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א יוֹנֶ֔ה חֲבֹלָת֥וֹ חוֹב֙ יָשִׁ֔יב גְּזֵלָ֖ה לֹ֣א יִגְזֹ֑ל לַחְמוֹ֙ לְרָעֵ֣ב יִתֵּ֔ן וְעֵירֹ֖ם יְכַסֶּה־ בָּֽגֶד׃

passages.text: He does not engage in usury or take excess interest, but he withholds his hand from iniquity and executes true justice between men.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man does not lend money for interest.
He does not take extra profit from others.
He keeps himself away from wrongdoing.
He judges honestly between one man and another.
passages.original: בַּנֶּ֣שֶׁךְ לֹֽא־ יִתֵּ֗ן וְתַרְבִּית֙ לֹ֣א יִקָּ֔ח מֵעָ֖וֶל יָשִׁ֣יב יָד֑וֹ מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ לְאִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: He follows My statutes and faithfully keeps My ordinances. That man is righteous; surely he will live, declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a righteous man.
This man follows God's statutes.
He keeps God's ordinances faithfully.
He does what is true and right.
This man is righteous.
God promises that this man will live.
The Lord GOD declares this.
passages.original: בְּחֻקּוֹתַ֧י יְהַלֵּ֛ךְ וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֥י שָׁמַ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֱמֶ֑ת צַדִּ֥יק הוּא֙ חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: Now suppose that man has a violent son, who sheds blood or does any of these things, though the father has done none of them: Indeed, the son eats at the mountain and defiles his neighbor’s wife.
passages.sermon:
A man has a son.
This son is violent.
This son sheds blood.
This son does evil things.
The father did not do these things.
The son eats at the mountain.
The son defiles his neighbor’s wife.
passages.original: וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן־ פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃ וְה֕וּא אֶת־ כָּל־ אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֑ה כִּ֣י גַ֤ם אֶל־ הֶֽהָרִים֙ אָכַ֔ל וְאֶת־ אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ טִמֵּֽא׃

passages.text: He oppresses the poor and needy; he commits robbery and does not restore a pledge. He lifts his eyes to idols; he commits abominations.
passages.sermon:
This man oppresses the poor.
He oppresses the needy.
He commits robbery.
He does not return what he took as a pledge.
He looks to idols.
He does abominable things.
passages.original: עָנִ֤י וְאֶבְיוֹן֙ הוֹנָ֔ה גְּזֵל֣וֹת גָּזָ֔ל חֲבֹ֖ל לֹ֣א יָשִׁ֑יב וְאֶל־ הַגִּלּוּלִים֙ נָשָׂ֣א עֵינָ֔יו תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: He engages in usury and takes excess interest. Will this son live? He will not! Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die; his blood will be on his own head.
passages.sermon:
This man is the son who does evil.
He gives money for interest.
He takes more than he should from others.
He lives in this way.
He will not live.
He has done all these evil things.
He will surely die.
He is responsible for his own death.
passages.original: בַּנֶּ֧שֶׁךְ נָתַ֛ן וְתַרְבִּ֥ית לָקַ֖ח וָחָ֑י לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הַתּוֹעֵב֤וֹת הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ עָשָׂ֔ה מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֔ת דָּמָ֖יו בּ֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Now suppose this son has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, considers them, and does not do likewise: He does not eat at the mountain or look to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor’s wife.
passages.sermon:
A man has a son.
This son sees all the sins his father has done.
He thinks about these sins.
He chooses not to do the same things.
He does not eat at the mountain shrines.
He does not look to the idols of the house of Israel.
He does not defile his neighbor’s wife.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֙ הוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וַיַּ֕רְא אֶת־ כָּל־ חַטֹּ֥את אָבִ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּרְאֶ֕ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כָּהֵֽן׃ עַל־ הֶֽהָרִים֙ לֹ֣א אָכָ֔ל וְעֵינָיו֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔א אֶל־ גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶת־ אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ לֹ֥א טִמֵּֽא׃

passages.text: He does not oppress another, or retain a pledge, or commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
passages.sermon:
This man does not oppress anyone.
He does not keep a pledge that belongs to another.
He does not rob anyone.
He gives his bread to the hungry.
He covers the naked with clothing.
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א הוֹנָ֔ה חֲבֹל֙ לֹ֣א חָבָ֔ל וּגְזֵלָ֖ה לֹ֣א גָזָ֑ל לַחְמוֹ֙ לְרָעֵ֣ב נָתָ֔ן וְעֵר֖וֹם כִּסָּה־ בָֽגֶד׃

passages.text: He withholds his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or usury. He keeps My ordinances and follows My statutes. Such a man will not die for his father’s iniquity. He will surely live.
passages.sermon:
This man does not harm the poor.
He does not take interest or usury.
He keeps God's ordinances.
He follows God's statutes.
He will not die for his father's sin.
He will surely live.
passages.original: מֵעָנִ֞י הֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ נֶ֤שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית֙ לֹ֣א לָקָ֔ח מִשְׁפָּטַ֣י עָשָׂ֔ה בְּחֻקּוֹתַ֖י הָלָ֑ךְ ה֗וּא לֹ֥א יָמ֛וּת בַּעֲוֺ֥ן אָבִ֖יו חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: As for his father, he will die for his own iniquity, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was wrong among his people.
passages.sermon:
The father acted with injustice.
He oppressed others.
He robbed his brother.
He did what was wrong among his people.
He will die for his own sin.
passages.original: אָבִ֞יו כִּֽי־ עָ֣שַׁק עֹ֗שֶׁק גָּזַל֙ גֵּ֣זֶל אָ֔ח וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ ט֛וֹב עָשָׂ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמָּ֑יו וְהִנֵּה־ מֵ֖ת בַּעֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Yet you may ask, ‘Why shouldn’t the son bear the iniquity of his father?’ Since the son has done what is just and right, carefully observing all My statutes, he will surely live.
passages.sermon:
The people may ask a question.
They may say, "Why does the son not bear the guilt of his father?"
The son does what is just.
The son does what is right.
The son keeps all of God's statutes.
The son obeys God's commands.
Because of this, the son will live.
He will not die for his father's sins.
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מַדֻּ֛עַ לֹא־ נָשָׂ֥א הַבֵּ֖ן בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֑ב וְהַבֵּ֞ן מִשְׁפָּ֧ט וּצְדָקָ֣ה עָשָׂ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־ חֻקּוֹתַ֥י שָׁמַ֛ר וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of his father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his son. The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.
passages.sermon:
God judges each person for their own actions.
The person who sins will die.
A son will not be punished for his father's sin.
A father will not be punished for his son's sin.
A righteous person will receive the reward for his righteousness.
A wicked person will receive the punishment for his wickedness.
passages.original: הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא־ יִשָּׂ֣א׀ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת רָשָׁע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man may do many sins.
He may turn away from all his sins.
He may keep all of God's statutes.
He may do what is just.
He may do what is right.
If he does these things, he will live.
He will not die.
passages.original: וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ מִכָּל־ חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְשָׁמַר֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ חֻקּוֹתַ֔י וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: None of the transgressions he has committed will be held against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
passages.sermon:
God judges each person for their own actions.
God does not hold a person's past sins against him if he turns from them.
If a person practices righteousness, God will not remember his past transgressions.
Because this person has done what is right, he will live.
passages.original: כָּל־ פְּשָׁעָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לֹ֥א יִזָּכְר֖וּ ל֑וֹ בְּצִדְקָת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Wouldn’t I prefer that he turn from his ways and live?
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD asks a question.
The Lord GOD does not enjoy the death of wicked people.
The Lord GOD prefers that wicked people turn from their evil ways.
The Lord GOD wants them to live.
passages.original: הֶחָפֹ֤ץ אֶחְפֹּץ֙ מ֣וֹת רָשָׁ֔ע נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה׃ס

passages.text: But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, committing the same abominations as the wicked, will he live? None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man is someone who does what is right in God’s eyes.
If a righteous man turns away from his righteousness, he stops doing what is right.
He then does what is evil.
He commits the same abominations that a wicked person does.
He acts just like the wicked.
He will not live because of this.
None of the righteous acts he did before will be remembered.
God will not count his past righteousness.
He has been unfaithful.
He has sinned.
Because of his unfaithfulness and sin, he will die.
passages.original: וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקָתוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל כְּכֹ֨ל הַתּוֹעֵב֜וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֧ה הָרָשָׁ֛ע יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה וָחָ֑י כָּל־ צִדְקָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂה֙ לֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֔רְנָה בְּמַעֲל֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ מָעַ֛ל וּבְחַטָּאת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָ֖א בָּ֥ם יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Hear now, O house of Israel: Is it My way that is unjust? Is it not your ways that are unjust?
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to the people of Israel.
The people say, "The way of the Lord is not just."
The Lord answers the house of Israel.
The Lord says, "Listen now, house of Israel."
The Lord asks, "Is it My way that is unjust?"
The Lord says, "It is your ways that are unjust."
passages.original: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י שִׁמְעוּ־ נָא֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲדַרְכִּי֙ לֹ֣א יִתָּכֵ֔ן הֲלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and practices iniquity, he will die for this. He will die because of the iniquity he has committed.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man lives by doing what is right.
If this righteous man turns away from his righteousness, he does wrong.
He commits iniquity.
He will die because of his wrongdoing.
He will die for the iniquity he has done.
passages.original: בְּשׁוּב־ צַדִּ֧יק מִצִּדְקָת֛וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה עָ֖וֶל וּמֵ֣ת עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם בְּעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֖ה יָמֽוּת׃ס

passages.text: But if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man does evil things.
He turns away from his wickedness.
He chooses to do what is just.
He chooses to do what is right.
He saves his own life.
passages.original: וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה ה֖וּא אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֥וֹ יְחַיֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Because he considered and turned from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
passages.sermon:
A man committed many transgressions.
He looked at his actions.
He thought about what he had done.
He turned away from all his transgressions.
He changed his ways.
He will surely live.
He will not die.
passages.original: וַיִּרְאֶ֣ה וַיָּשׁוֹב מִכָּל־ פְּשָׁעָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה חָי֥וֹ יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ Are My ways unjust, O house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unjust?
passages.sermon:
The house of Israel speaks.
They say, "The way of the Lord is not just."
God responds to the house of Israel.
God asks, "Are My ways unjust, house of Israel?"
God says, "Your ways are unjust, not Mine."
passages.original: וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י הַדְּרָכַ֞י לֹ֤א יִתָּֽכְנּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵֽן׃

passages.text: Therefore, O house of Israel, I will judge you, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent and turn from all your transgressions, so that your iniquity will not become your downfall.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks to the house of Israel.
He says, "I will judge each person in Israel according to his own ways."
Repent from your sins.
Turn away from all your transgressions.
If you do this, your iniquity will not cause your downfall.
passages.original: לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה שׁ֤וּבוּ וְהָשִׁ֙יבוּ֙ מִכָּל־ פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם לְמִכְשׁ֖וֹל עָוֺֽן׃

passages.text: Cast away from yourselves all the transgressions you have committed, and fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, O house of Israel?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the house of Israel.
God commands the people of Israel.
Remove all your sins from yourselves.
You have committed these sins.
Make a new heart for yourselves.
Make a new spirit for yourselves.
Why should you die, house of Israel?
passages.original: הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֗ם אֶת־ כָּל־ פִּשְׁעֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֣ם בָּ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם לֵ֥ב חָדָ֖שׁ וְר֣וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלָ֥מָּה תָמֻ֖תוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, declares the Lord GOD. So repent and live!
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord GOD does not want anyone to die.
The Lord GOD takes no pleasure in the death of any person.
Repent.
Turn back from your wrong ways.
Live.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הַמֵּ֔ת נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ׃פ
